title: Mastering Programme Management: A Step-by-Step Guide
author: The Effective Project Manager
summary: This step-by-step guide explains programme management as the coordination of multiple interrelated projects towards strategic organisational goals, as distinct from managing a single project. It moves through preparation, execution and monitoring, centring on a Programme Management Plan covering scope, governance, stakeholder engagement, budget, staffing, communication and risk. The most useful advice is concrete: budgets should span at least three years, roles must be clear, senior stakeholders should not undermine lower-level managers, and dashboards should spare project teams duplicate reporting. It also stresses that programme risks are usually organisational, that change control should treat reversible changes lightly, and that the aim of addressing issues is to solve them, not to chastise individuals. The piece is generic in tone but offers a usable management checklist for leaders overseeing complex, multi-team work.
points: Programme management differs from project management by keeping a view of how projects fit together to deliver value, not just delivering each one.
Unclear roles and senior stakeholders overriding junior managers are named as common causes of conflict and mishaps.
Reporting should be consolidated through dashboards so busy project teams do not give the same information to several audiences.
Programme-level risks tend to be organisational, such as solvency, senior staffing and political environment, and deserve dedicated attention.
When problems recur, the guidance is to solve the issue and consider training rather than blame the individual.
quotes: Programme management is a discipline that coordinates and aligns multiple interrelated projects with the aim of achieving strategic business objectives. Unlike project management, which focuses on the execution of individual projects, programme management deals with the holistic view of how various projects fit together to deliver value to an organization.
The budget should be presented at a high level and span multiple years. At least the next three years should always have clear budgets.
Define which topics warrant formal written communication and which may benefit from more informal communication. Remember that the aim is not to create admin, but to ensure efficiency in management.

Unclear roles are the cause of many project/programme mishaps. Ensure that senior stakeholders understand that their authority should not be used to undermine the authority of lower-rung managers. This is a sure manner in which to cause conflict.

Try to establish dashboards which can be used to monitor progress against multiple indicators easily. Project teams are already busy with their ow reporting and it is counter-productive to ask them to report the same information again to multiple sources.
Always remember that the goal of addressing issues is to solve the issue, not to chastise the individual. If there are errors which repeatedly manifest, consider training interventions.

Programmatic risks are often organisational risks. They may relate to macro issues such as business solvency, high level human resources (such as senior management), economic issues, legislative or political environments.
